fact: Monte Cielo's design guidelines define landscaping to include turf alongside patios, decks, retaining walls, water features, ponds and swimming pools, and set a design intent of natural, informal plant groupings using native or hardy materials.
quote: The design intent of the Monte Cielo master landscape plan and overall theme of development in Monte Cielo is that of natural and informal groupings of plant materials in order to unify Monte Cielo into a cohesive neighborhood. To the greatest extent possible, utilizing natural landform and native or hardy landscape materials is encouraged. Landscaping includes, but is not limited to, trees, shrubs, turf, planting areas and gardens, patios, decks, retaining wall structures, "hard sculptures", gazebos, arbors, water features, ponds, swimming pools and other such items.
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Sec. 12.1 Design Intent
notes: Read in full 2026-09-26 (19-page recorded copy posted by Flagstaff Management; text layer checked against the page images for Secs. 6, 12.4-12.9). Neither the guidelines, the declaration nor the Design Review Request form uses the words artificial, synthetic or putting green. The posted copy ends at page 19 and does not include Appendices A-F (submittal requirements, forms, fee schedule, final landscape plan contents).

fact: Monte Cielo requires landscaping to follow a professionally prepared plan by a qualified professional with Colorado experience, highly encourages a landscape architect, and requires the Design Review Committee to approve the final landscape plan before installation.
quote: Landscaping shall be installed pursuant to a professionally prepared landscaping plan prepared by a qualified professional with experience in the State of Colorado. The use of a qualified Landscape Architect is highly encouraged. A Final Landscape Plan (as described in Appendix E), indicating location and numbers of plantings, location of plant beds, berms, fences (including typical sections of all fence types) and other information as required to demonstrate compliance with these Design Guidelines shall be approved by the Committee prior to installation of landscaping.
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Sec. 12.2 Landscaping Plan

fact: A Monte Cielo landscape plan must show every proposed landscaping improvement, turf, patios, built-in barbecues, pools and water features among them, with a general description of the irrigation system and the lot's building envelope lines.
quote: The landscape plan shall include all proposed landscaping improvements including: fences, shrubs, turf, planting areas and gardens, patios, mulches (bark, gravel, etc.), landscape structures (decks, retaining walls, gazebos, arbors, built-in barbecues, etc.), swimming pools, ornamental features (water features, statuary, etc.), garden areas and any other such feature, as well as a general description of the irrigation system. … In addition, landscape plans shall include property lines and building envelope lines, easements, ancillary structures, accessory buildings, locations of special areas to be screened with either fences or vegetation and service line locations.
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Sec. 12.2 Landscaping Plan

fact: Monte Cielo's guidelines require every area not in shrub beds, garden beds, acceptable ground cover, patios, decks or other hard surfaces to be sodded with Kentucky bluegrass, a mostly bluegrass mix or other grasses the Design Review Committee approves.
quote: All areas not in shrub beds, designated garden/flower bed areas, areas planted with acceptable ground cover materials, patios, decks or other hard surface areas shall be sodded with a Kentucky Bluegrass or a predominately Kentucky Bluegrass mixture or other grasses approved by the Design Review Committee. (Seed for turf areas may be utilized with special approval of the Committee).
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Sec. 12.9.f Minimum Plant Material Quantities
notes: The same section sets minimum plantings: two 2-inch caliper trees and ten 5-gallon shrubs in the front yard, one 2-inch caliper tree in the rear yard, and five 5-gallon shrubs in a back or side bed visible from adjacent lots or streets (12.9.a-e). Read with co-hoa-backyard-detached for back yards.

fact: In Monte Cielo, changes to a lot or its landscaping after the home is complete and occupied go through Special Review with the application form and three copies of the plans, and the committee refers a proposal to the adjacent owners for comment if it thinks it could adversely affect them.
quote: The purpose of the Special Review process is to review those special items that are more Lot specific than these general guidelines can address in detail. This Special Review process includes any modifications to the Lot or landscaping, except building additions that occur after the residence is complete and occupied. Contents of the submittal information shall include the application form included in Appendix B along with a minimum of three (3) copies of all information required to adequately describe the proposal. If, in the opinion of the Committee, the proposal could adversely impact adjacent property owners, it will be referred to them for comment.
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Sec. 6 Special Review
notes: Checked against the page image (recorded page 6 of 19).

fact: Monte Cielo's guidelines let a designated Committee Executive review minor landscaping projects at an executive level, but require committee approval before work starts on any reconfiguration of the landscape architecture.
quote: Minor applications may include, but are not limited to, minor non-structural changes to the exterior of a building (i.e., color changes to exterior paint or stain on a structure), temporary signage (including real estate signs), and minor landscaping projects which are not a part of a previously approved landscape plan or specifically exempted above. … All structural changes, remodeling and reconfigurations of the architecture and/or landscape architecture shall be reviewed and Committee approval must be received before work commences.
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Sec. 4.4 Executive Level Approval
notes: Whether a lawn-to-turf conversion or a putting green is 'minor' is not defined; the Committee Executive decides in writing and may refer any application to the full committee.

fact: Monte Cielo's declaration gives the Design Review Committee 30 days to decide a complete application, but the period starts only when the committee signs a written Decision Period Notice, which it must issue only on the applicant's written request, and a request is deemed approved if nothing comes back within 30 days of that notice.
quote: The decision of the Committee shall be made in writing within thirty (30) days after receipt by the Committee of a completed application, all materials required under the Design Review Guidelines, and all other materials or information required or requested by the Committee (the "Decision Period") as set forth in this paragraph. The Decision Period will not commence to run unless and until the Committee has executed a written acknowledgement that the thirty (30) day decision period has commenced (the "Decision Period Notice"), and the Committee shall have no obligation to issue a Decision Period Notice except on written request of the Applicant. … Any request for approval of a proposed Improvement shall be deemed approved if the Committee has not issued a decision or made written request for further information within thirty (30) days of the Decision Period Notice.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo (formerly known as Blue Mountain Vista), recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Paragraphs 7.7 and 7.9
notes: Checked against the page images (recorded pages 30-31 of 65). A written request for more information, or any new submission, ends a Decision Period Notice; a new notice must then issue.

fact: Under Monte Cielo's declaration the applicant or any Impacted Owner may appeal a committee decision to the Board within 10 days, and the applicant may not start work until that 10-day window has passed or, if an appeal is filed, until the Final Decision.
quote: Except where the Board of Directors has acted as the Committee, any decision of the Committee may be appealed to the Board of Directors by (i) the Applicant and/or (ii) any Impacted Owner. To initiate such an appeal, the appealing Party shall provide written notice of such appeal to the Board of Directors and the Committee within ten (10) days after the delivery of the decision of the Committee to the Applicant as set forth above. … An Applicant may not proceed with any construction activity or work on any Improvement on the Lot until the expiration of the ten (10) day period within which an appeal may be initiated and if an appeal has been initiated may not proceed until a Final Decision has been issued.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo, recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Paragraph 7.8
notes: 'Impacted Owner' is not defined in the declaration's Article One (searched the full OCR text).

fact: Monte Cielo's design guidelines describe a different appeal: an owner writes to the committee itself within 30 calendar days, is heard at a meeting, and gets the committee's written decision within seven days, which is final.
quote: If an Owner wishes to appeal any decision of the Committee, the Owner may do so by submitting a written appeal to the Committee within thirty (30) calendar days of the original Committee decision. The Committee will then schedule a meeting with the Owner at which time the appeal will be reviewed. The Owner will have the opportunity to be heard by the Committee prior to the Committee rendering a final decision. Within seven (7) days of the decision regarding the appeal request, the Committee shall give notice in writing of their decision to the Owner. All decisions of the Committee shall be final.
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Sec. 8 Appeal Procedures
notes: Conflicts with declaration Paragraph 7.8 (appeal to the Board within 10 days). The guidelines say they supplement, not supersede, the declaration.

fact: Monte Cielo's Design Review Request form, which lists landscaping as an improvement type, says the committee has 30 days from the request's receipt date, that approval does not relieve the owner of building permits from the City of Longmont if required, and that the project must be completed within one year.
quote: I understand that I must obtain approval of the Association before I commence any improvements. I understand that, per the Covenants Monte Cielo HOA, the committee has 30 days from the receipt date of the request to come to a decision. I understand that Association approval does not relieve me of my responsibility to obtain building permits from the City of Longmont, if required. … (Project must be completed within 1 year)
source_label: Monte Cielo HOA, Design Review Request (one-page form, c/o Flagstaff Management, Inc.)
notes: The form is undated. Its City of Longmont permit line and its 30-days-from-receipt clock differ from the recorded declaration (Paragraphs 7.7, 7.20: county permits; Decision Period Notice) and from the county parcel records, which list every Monte Cielo lot as unincorporated.

fact: Flagstaff Management, which manages Monte Cielo from Longmont, says a Design Review Request Form is required for all improvements and that the committee has 30 days to decide.
quote: A Design Review Request Form is required to be turned in for all improvements. The committee has 30 days to make a decision, so please plan accordingly.
source_label: Flagstaff Management, Monte Cielo community page (Architecture & Landscape)
notes: The page lists 2026 meetings on March 16 and July 20 as cancelled and the annual meeting on November 16, 2026, and says budget, financials and minutes are sent on request (none posted).

fact: As of September 26, 2026, Flagstaff Management's Monte Cielo page posts the governance documents, design guidelines, design review form, resolutions and policies, and no preapproved water-wise front-yard designs.
quote: Governance: Articles of Incorporation · Bylaws · Covenants, Conditions & Restrictions · Design Guidelines. Architecture & Landscape: View Design Review Request Form & Instructions. Reserve Study & Resolutions: Resolutions · Adoption of Policies, Procedures & Rules · Alternative Dispute Resolution · Collection Policy · Conduct of Meetings · Conflict of Interest · Covenants & Rule Enforcement Policy · Enforcement Policy · Inspection Policy · Reserve Study Policy
source_label: Flagstaff Management, Monte Cielo community page, document list read September 26, 2026
notes: The quote lists the page's document headings and link titles in order. The Adoption of Policies, Procedures & Rules and the Covenant & Rule Enforcement PDFs are image-only scans; their titles do not suggest landscape designs. Budget, financials and minutes are sent on request only.

fact: A Monte Cielo approval expires if substantial work has not begun within 12 months of the Final Decision, and approved work must be finished within 12 months of starting and within 24 months of the Final Decision.
quote: Unless a substantial amount of work on the Approved Improvements has been commenced and diligently pursued within twelve (12) months of the Final Decision, the Final Decision shall expire on the date that is twelve (12) months from the date of the Final Decision unless extended by the written approval of the Committee. … Unless the Final Decision expressly extends the period for completion, all Approved Improvements shall be completed within twelve (12) months of the commencement of any construction and within twenty-four (24) months of the Final Decision.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo, recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Paragraph 7.10
notes: Design Guidelines Sec. 5.6 says the same (one year to act; 12 months from commencement; 24 months from final approval).

fact: Monte Cielo's declaration lets the Design Review Committee set application fees by type and scope of project and make an applicant pay the consultant costs of reviewing that application.
quote: The Committee shall determine the amount of the application fee and may establish different amounts and categories of fees for different types or scopes of Improvements as it deems appropriate. The Committee may engage consultants as it deems necessary to assist the Committee in the performance of its duties and may, as part of the application fee or otherwise, require that any Applicant pay the consultant costs related to that application.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo, recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Paragraph 7.4
notes: Design Guidelines Sec. 7 says the current fee schedule is attached as Appendix D; the posted 19-page copy has no appendices, and no fee appears on the request form or the management page.

fact: Monte Cielo's declaration allows no improvement on a lot outside the building envelope Boulder County approved for it, except what the county specifically allowed outside it.
quote: All Improvements shall comply with the County's land use and zoning requirements or building code and with the Design Guidelines. No Improvements shall be placed or erected on any Lot except within the designated building envelope for the Lot approved by the County except for such Improvements as are specifically allowed to be constructed outside of the building envelope as approved by the County.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo, recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Paragraph 8.3
notes: Design Guidelines Sec. 10.4: all improvements within the building envelope as designated on the Final Plats. The envelopes are drawn on the recorded plats (Filing One, July 11, 2005; Filing Two, June 22, 2007), which are not posted online.

fact: Monte Cielo's declaration counts grading and any change of grade or drainage pattern, and landscaping features from sprinkler systems, retaining walls and sod to gravel and exterior lighting fixtures, as Improvements.
quote: IMPROVEMENTS means: … (c) the grading, excavation, filling, or similar disturbance to the surface of the land including, without limitation, change of grade, change of ground level, change of drainage pattern; (d) all landscaping features, including, but not limited to, patios, patio covers, awnings, or other finish materials on any visible structure, walkways, sprinkler systems, fences, screening walls, retaining walls, decks, hedges, windbreaks, trees, shrubs, flowers, sod and all other plantings, gravel, bark, exterior lighting fixtures, poles, signs
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo, recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Paragraph 1.26

fact: Monte Cielo allows basketball hoops, playground equipment, clotheslines, wood piles and storage only inside a lot's building envelope and only with Design Review Committee approval, and puts landscaping and exterior lighting under the committee too.
quote: No basketball hoops, poles or backboards, other playground equipment, clotheslines, wood piles, or storage areas or containers may be installed on any Lot except within the building envelope approved for the Lot and unless approved by the Design Review Committee in accordance with Article Seven of this Declaration … Porch and area lighting, property identification, landscaping, or other exterior improvements on any Lot shall be subject to the Design Guidelines and the approval of the Design Review Committee in accordance with Article Seven of this Declaration
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo, recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Paragraph 8.19
notes: Design Guidelines Sec. 10.12: play equipment only within the building envelope; where visible from public streets it may go in a screened or fenced area the committee approves.

fact: In Monte Cielo every landscaped area with plant materials inside the building envelope, plus the front strip between the envelope and the street, must have automatic irrigation, while the rest of the lot outside the envelope need not be irrigated but must be mowed and kept free of noxious weeds.
quote: Each and every Lot shall be provided with an automatic irrigation system capable of watering all landscaped areas within the building envelope containing plant materials to ensure the continued survival of plant materials within the building envelope. The irrigation system shall also supply water to any portion of the Lot outside of the building envelope that is between the front line of the building envelope on the Lot and the street that the home faces. … Except as provided above in this Section 12.4, areas on the Lot outside of building envelope are not required to be irrigated but must mowed regularly and maintained free of noxious weeds and other unsightly growth.
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Sec. 12.4 Irrigation System
notes: Checked against the page image (recorded page 18 of 19). The section also asks that irrigation be designed to minimize overspray and conserve water, with head placement shown on the final landscape plan.

fact: Monte Cielo's declaration requires grasses inside the building envelope and out to the street to be mowed and weed-free, and all landscaping to be irrigated enough to stay green and thriving.
quote: Any grasses within the building envelope on the lot and between the building envelope and the street fronting the Lot shall be regularly mowed and kept free of noxious and unsightly weeds in accordance with the Design Guidelines. Landscaping including but not limited to trees, shrubs, grasses and other plants shall be properly and sufficiently irrigated so as to be kept in a green and thriving condition.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo, recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Paragraph 8.5

fact: Monte Cielo's guidelines require any strip between curb and sidewalk to be planted in grass, sprinkled and kept up by the owner, and the front area outside the envelope to be watered enough to stay green and growing.
quote: That portion of the Lot outside of the building envelope that is between the front line of the building envelope on the Lot and the street that the home faces shall also be maintained in a similar fashion, with sufficient water to maintain the area in a green and growing condition. … The space between the back of the curb and the edge of the sidewalk, if any, shall be planted in grass and sprinkled and maintained by the home owner.
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Secs. 12.6 and 12.8

fact: Monte Cielo bars general area floodlights except for temporary seasonal displays, keeps exterior light from being aimed outside the building envelope, and encourages low-voltage ground lights for decorative site lighting.
quote: Exterior lighting shall not be directed in such a manner as to create an annoyance to adjoining properties and shall not be directed outside the building envelope on a Lot. Exterior lighting shall also consider light pollution and be screened accordingly. The use of unshielded or globular luminaries is prohibited. General area floodlights are expressly prohibited, unless used with colored lights as part of a temporary, seasonal lighting display and directed toward the residence on the Lot. The use of low-voltage, "ground light," for decorative site lighting, is encouraged.
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Sec. 10.11 Exterior Lighting
notes: Declaration Paragraph 8.7 separately bars light that is unreasonably bright or causes unreasonable glare.

fact: Monte Cielo's guidelines ask that landscaping be designed to keep views to the mountains into and out of neighboring lots where possible, and warn that large evergreens block views year round while deciduous trees open them in winter.
quote: Distant and close-in views looking into and out of adjacent sites to mountains should be maintained where possible and landscaping should be designed to maintain the same. … Landscaping design should keep in mind view corridor recommendations as outlined herein; specifically with location of ultimately tall trees and, more importantly, ultimately large evergreens. (Deciduous trees allow views in the winter months while evergreen trees would block views year round).
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Secs. 10.3.b and 12.2
notes: Sec. 3 puts the burden on the owner proposing construction to show that adjacent view corridors stay reasonable; declaration Paragraph 7.6 lists impacts on views from other lots among the committee's review criteria.

fact: Monte Cielo exempts a permanently mounted gas-fired barbecue from committee review when it is in the backyard inside the building envelope, while arbors, patio covers, gazebos, cabanas and swimming pools all need committee approval.
quote: The following types of changes, additions or alterations do not require approval of the Committee: … Installation of permanently mounted gas-fired barbecues so long as these are installed in the backyard in the building envelope. … Ancillary structures, such as greenhouses, arbors, patio covers, cabanas, gazebos, swimming pools, etc., shall be sited and designed to be compatible with the residence and/or fences. All such items will require Committee approval.
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Secs. 4.3.h and 10.13

fact: Monte Cielo allows no fence outside the building envelope, limits perimeter fencing to wood open rail no higher than 4 feet, and allows a wood privacy fence of up to 6 feet around part of a backyard only inside the envelope, at least 6 feet behind the front facade line and with written committee approval.
quote: All perimeter fencing shall be of the open rail type and must be constructed of wood. Fences are not allowed outside of the building envelope on a Lot. … Perimeter fence rails shall not be higher than four feet (4') above finish grade. … Privacy and screening fences may be constructed within a building envelope to enclose a portion of the backyard for a house and must be located at least six feet (6') behind the front façade line of the house and only with the written approval of the Committee. Privacy and screening fences shall be no more than six feet (6') high
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Sec. 10.8 Fencing
notes: Rectangle wire mesh (2x4, 9 gauge galvanized) may go on the lot side of the open rail to contain pets and small children. Chain link, pipe rails and exposed metal posts are prohibited.

fact: Monte Cielo's landscape guidelines allow berms only where they read as natural landforms, bar berms that block drainage or push it toward neighbors or foundations, call for a 10% slope away from the house for at least 10 feet, and require grading to match the community's master grading and drainage plans.
quote: Natural drainage patterns must be respected. The use of berms is encouraged only if continuous expanses of landform are created which look natural as opposed to looking man-made. Berms should not obstruct drainage channels, divert drainage onto adjacent properties or toward building foundations. Finish grading should be designed to: avoid ponding on the site; allow 10% slopes away from the residence for a distance of at least 10 feet; avoid excessive run-off at a point onto adjacent sites; and maintain existing drainage patterns/channels. Grading plans must conform to the approved Master Grading and Drainage Plans prepared for Monte Cielo, copies of which are available upon request. The final landscape plan shall indicate contours and/or finish grade elevations showing and assuring that the proper drainage is indicated and retained through the construction of the landscape.
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Sec. 12.3 Grading Drainage

fact: Monte Cielo's declaration bars any interference with the drainage pattern the developer established unless the Board approves it in writing with adequate alternate drainage, and requires any proposed change to be prepared, signed and stamped by a Colorado professional engineer.
quote: There shall be no interference with the established drainage pattern initially established by Declarant over any portion of the Planned Community, except as approved in writing by the Board of Directors. Approval shall not be granted unless provision is made for adequate alternate drainage. … Any proposed alteration to the drainage pattern must be prepared, signed and stamped by a qualified Professional Engineer registered in the State of Colorado.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo, recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Paragraph 11.4
notes: The established drainage pattern may run from common areas over a lot, from a lot over common areas and from one lot over another.

fact: Monte Cielo's declaration discloses that the community's soils are potentially expansive and its water table potentially high, and tells owners to investigate what that means for anything they build.
quote: DECLARANT HEREBY DISCLOSES TO ALL OWNERS OF LOTS IN THE PLANNED COMMUNITY THAT THE SOILS ARE POTENTIALLY EXPANSIVE AND THE WATER TABLE IS POTENTIALLY HIGH WITHIN THE PLANNED COMMUNITY. ALL OWNERS ARE HEREBY ADVISED TO INVESTIGATE THE CONSEQUENCES AND IMPACTS OF SUCH PHYSICAL CHARACTERISTICS ON ANY IMPROVEMENTS CONSTRUCTED ON ANY LOTS IN THE PLANNED COMMUNITY.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo, recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Paragraph 8.25
notes: The paragraph goes on to say sellers of a vacant lot or new home are expected to give buyers the disclosures C.R.S. 6-6.5-101 requires, including a soils report (shared record co-new-home-soils-report).

fact: The Monte Cielo association maintains any irrigation ditch on any of its outlots or any lot, whoever owns the ditch, as a common expense.
quote: In addition to the Common Areas required to be maintained by the Association as set forth above, the Association shall maintain any irrigation ditches that are located on any of the Outlots or any of the Lots in the Planned Community, regardless of the ownership of the ditches. The cost to the Association of this maintenance shall be a Common Expense of the Association.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo, recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Paragraph 3.1
notes: Which lots, if any, a ditch crosses is shown on the recorded plats and easements (Exhibit C lists plats of July 11, 2005 and June 22, 2007), not in the posted documents.

fact: The Monte Cielo association owns and maintains outlots reserved for open space, landscaping, drainage and detention ponds, outlots reserved for trails and open space, and the private road Strawberry Circle.
quote: Outlot B, Block 1, Blue Mountain Vista TDR/PUD Filing No. One is reserved for open space, landscaping, drainage and detention pond facilities and will be owned and maintained by the Association. The trail located within this Outlot shall be owned and maintained by the Association. Outlot D, Block 1, Blue Mountain Vista TDR/PUD Filing No. One is reserved for open space, landscaping, drainage and detention pond facilities and will be owned and maintained by the Association. … Outlot A, Block 1, Blue Mountain Vista TDR/PUD Filing No. Two is a private right of way for the road known as Strawberry Circle to provide access to the Planned Community and will be owned and maintained by the Association. … Outlot B, Block 1, Blue Mountain Vista TDR/PUD Filing No. Two is reserved for trails, open space, and utilities and will be owned and maintained by the Association.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo, recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Paragraph 3.1
notes: Outlot C of Filing Two is also reserved for trails, open space, utilities and emergency access. Outlot C of Filing One was held by the declarant with a right to convey it to the Hygiene Fire Protection District.

fact: Monte Cielo, formerly called Blue Mountain Vista, is a planned community of 22 lots: the original seven plus 15 added by the 2012 amended and restated declaration.
quote: The number of Lots initially submitted to the Planned Community by the Original Declaration was seven (7). In addition to those original seven (7) lots, this Declaration submits fifteen (15) more lots to the Planned Community; therefore as of the recording of this Declaration there are twenty-two (22) Lots submitted to the Planned Community.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo (formerly known as Blue Mountain Vista), recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Paragraph 2.3

fact: Monte Cielo's declaration submits the community to the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act and limits every dwelling to single-family residential use.
quote: NOW THEREFORE, by this Declaration the Property described on Exhibit A and Exhibit B attached hereto, together with all easements, rights, and appurtenances thereto and improvements thereon is submitted to the provisions of the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act … no Dwelling Unit within the Planned Community shall be used for any purpose other than single-family residential purposes.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo, recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Preamble and Paragraph 8.2

fact: Monte Cielo's design guidelines supplement Boulder County's land use and building regulations, with the more stringent rule applying where they conflict, and neither the guidelines nor the declaration mentions the City of Longmont.
quote: They do not supersede, but rather supplement the Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions (the "Declaration") for Monte Cielo, and the land use and building regulations of Boulder County, Colorado (the "County"), which may govern the development of the single family residences and related Improvements in Monte Cielo. Where the Design Guidelines and the Declaration are in conflict with the County Regulations, the more stringent requirements shall apply.
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Sec. 1 Purpose
notes: Both documents searched in full (OCR text) for Longmont on 2026-09-26: no match. Declaration Paragraph 7.20: the applicant is responsible to apply and pay for all permits and approvals required by the County.

fact: Monte Cielo's declaration makes committee approval an addition to any review and approval the county requires, and makes the applicant responsible to apply and pay for every permit and approval the county requires.
quote: This approval of the Committee is in addition to any required review and approval by the County. … The Applicant shall be responsible to apply and pay for all permits and approvals required by the County.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo, recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Paragraphs 7.1 and 7.20
notes: The declaration defines the County: "COUNTY means Boulder County, Colorado." (Paragraph 1.16).

fact: Boulder County's parcel map lists all 22 residential lots of Blue Mountain Vista Filings 1 and 2 on Strawberry Circle as unincorporated, drawn at about 43,500 to 68,800 square feet, roughly 1 to 1.6 acres, each.

fact: Boulder County's Land Use Code applies to all land in unincorporated Boulder County, and neither its current text (updated May 13, 2025) nor the amendments adopted by Resolution 2026-011 uses the word turf.
quote: This Code shall apply to all land within the unincorporated areas of Boulder County.
source_label: Boulder County Land Use Code (current version updated May 13, 2025), Sec. 1-400 Jurisdiction and Authority; full 496-page text searched for "turf"
notes: Searched 2026-09-26: 'turf' appears nowhere in the 496-page Land Use Code PDF or in Resolution 2026-011 (DC-25-0003, approved January 15, 2026, signed March 24, 2026), which reprints the amended articles. HB25-1113 requires counties to regulate live turf in new residential development by January 1, 2028 (co-hb25-1113-residential-live-turf-2028).

fact: Boulder County's most recent Land Use Code amendments, docket DC-25-0003, were approved January 15, 2026 and signed as Resolution 2026-011, covering minor corrections, clarifications and updates to comply with state law, without any turf provision.
quote: A resolution approving Boulder County Community Planning & Permitting Docket DC-25-0003: Text Amendments to the Land Use Code Related to Minor Corrections, Clarifying Changes, and Updates to Comply with State Law
source_label: Boulder County Resolution 2026-011 (Docket DC-25-0003; BOCC hearing January 15, 2026)
notes: The text layer (about 215,000 words) was searched for 'turf': no match. 'Artificial' appears only in 'natural and artificial drainage ways'.

fact: Boulder County issues building permits for unincorporated Boulder County and lists swimming pools, decks, retaining walls over 48 inches and fences over six feet high among the additions that need one.
quote: The Community Planning and Permitting Department issues building permits for unincorporated areas of Boulder County. If your property is inside a city or town, please contact the city or town directly. … Additions: Examples include but are not limited to: buildings, swimming pools, decks, retaining walls over 48 inches, and fences over six feet high.
source_label: Boulder County Community Planning & Permitting, Building Permits (When Do You Need a Building Permit?)
notes: The same page says the current Boulder County Building Code Amendments took effect July 1, 2026 and apply to the unincorporated county. Laying turf is not on its list of examples.

fact: Boulder County's Land Use Code offers the TDR/PUD, the kind of plat Monte Cielo sits on, as an alternative to annexation into a city for development.
quote: In addition to those purposes outlined within these Regulations, NUPUD, NCNUPUD, and TDR/PUD submission, review, and action shall be guided by the following objectives: … To offer the NUPUD and TDR/PUD processes as a viable alternative to municipal annexation for development purposes.
source_label: Boulder County Land Use Code (current version updated May 13, 2025), Sec. 6-100.D.4
notes: Monte Cielo's documents name its plat the Blue Mountain Vista TDR/PUD (Transferred Development Rights Planned Unit Development).

fact: In Monte Cielo a pet outdoors on a lot and off leash must be kept in a pen screened from view from the street, other lots and common areas and approved by the Design Review Committee.
quote: Except when the pet is on a leash and being directly controlled by its owner or caretaker, any pet that is outdoors on a Lot shall be kept in a pen that is screened from view from the street and any other Lot or Common Area in the Planned Community and has been approved by the Design Review Committee in accordance with the Design Review Guidelines.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Monte Cielo, recorded in Boulder County July 13, 2012, reception 03236442, Paragraph 8.15

fact: Monte Cielo allows dog runs that are not a nuisance, requires them to be kept free of pet waste and odor, and requires each run to be drawn on the landscape plan, screened to the fencing standards and approved in location before construction.
quote: Dog runs are allowed so long as they are not a nuisance to the neighbors, either visually or due to excessive noise and barking or odor. Dog runs and related yards shall be kept clean and free of pet waste and odor at all times. Dog runs shall be located on the required landscape plans and the screening shall conform to the fencing and screening standards. Location of dog runs must be approved by the Committee before construction begins.
source_label: Design Guidelines of Monte Cielo (adopted as of July 12, 2012; recorded in Boulder County April 16, 2015, reception 03440127), Sec. 10.9.b Dog runs
